title: Horizontal and vertical homotopy components for Cartan--Eilenberg comparison maps
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $K^\bullet$ and $L^\bullet$ be cochain complexes in $\mathcal A$, and let $I^{\bullet,\bullet}$ and $J^{\bullet,\bullet}$ be first-quadrant double complexes with augmentations $\epsilon_I:K^\bullet\to I^{\bullet,0}$ and $\epsilon_J:L^\bullet\to J^{\bullet,0}$. For each horizontal degree $p$, write $B_I^p$, $Z_I^p$, and $H_I^p$ for the boundary, cycle, and horizontal-cohomology row complexes of $I$, and similarly for $J$; assume the augmented $B_I$, $Z_I$, and $H_I$ rows (and their exact sequences, including $0\to Z_I^p\to I^{p,\bullet}\to B_I^{p+1}\to0$) are exact resolutions, while the corresponding augmented $B_J$, $Z_J$, and $H_J$ rows are injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $\delta:I\to J$ be a morphism of double complexes. Suppose a complex map $w:K^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ and maps $s^p:K^p\to L^{p-1}$ satisfy $w^p=d_L^{p-1}s^p+s^{p+1}d_K^p$ and $\delta^{p,0}\epsilon_I^p=\epsilon_J^p w^p$ for every $p$. Then there exist maps $s_1^{p,q}:I^{p,q}\to J^{p-1,q}$ and $s_2^{p,q}:I^{p,q}\to J^{p,q-1}$, zero outside the first quadrant, such that $s_1^{p,0}\epsilon_I^p=\epsilon_J^{p-1}s^p$ and, with $H^{p,q}=s_1^{p,q}+(-1)^p s_2^{p,q}$, one has $d_{\operatorname{Tot}J}H+Hd_{\operatorname{Tot}I}=\delta$ for the total-complex convention [def-sp-double-complex-total]. The resulting homotopy satisfies $H(F^q\operatorname{Tot}^n)\subseteq F^{q-1}\operatorname{Tot}^{n-1}$ for the decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration] by vertical degree.

source.place: Remark Tag 015K (functoriality) together with the comparison construction of Lemma Tag 015I; horizontal/vertical decomposition is the Cartan--Eilenberg homotopy argument (Weibel, Homological Algebra, Lemma 5.7.10)

proof.text: Apply the horizontal comparison construction to the exact source rows and injective target rows. The augmentation identity and the given null-homotopy w = d_L s + s d_K give maps s1 with the prescribed augmentation identity, and the residual R = delta - d_h s1 - s1 d_h is a vertical-complex map whose augmented horizontal row is zero.

source.place: Lemma 015I comparison construction by boundary, cycle, and cohomology rows; Weibel Homological Algebra Lemma 5.7.10

proof.text: The residual map vanishes on the augmentation and is a morphism of double complexes: it commutes with d_h because delta does and d_h(d_hs_1+s_1d_h)=d_hs_1d_h=(d_hs_1+s_1d_h)d_h, and with d_v because delta and s_1 do. So the comparison theorem on the boundary, cycle, and horizontal-cohomology row resolutions supplies the row null-homotopies and the vertical child assembles them through the exact sequences into maps s2, zero in vertical degree zero, with R = d_v s2 + s2 d_v and s2 commuting with the horizontal differentials.

source.place: Lemma 015I compatibility with the second exact sequence and vertical differential; Weibel Homological Algebra Lemma 5.7.10

proof.text: Define H^{p,q}=s_1^{p,q}+(-1)^p s_2^{p,q}. Expanding d_Tot=d_h+(-1)^p d_v gives the three component identities: in bidegree (p,q), d_hs_1+s_1d_h=delta-d_vs_2-s_2d_v; in bidegree (p+1,q-1), s_2d_h=d_hs_2; and in bidegree (p-1,q+1), s_1d_v=d_vs_1. The first is the definition of R together with the vertical identity, the second is the horizontal compatibility of s2, and the third is the column-complex property of s1, so d_Tot H+Hd_Tot=delta.

The component s1 preserves vertical degree and s2 lowers it by one; therefore the resulting homotopy sends the q-th filtration piece in total degree n into the (q-1)-st piece in degree n-1. First-quadrant boundedness makes all total sums finite.
